address_pairs.notes: Al Diab repeatedly addresses the masked protagonist as 젊은이 while attempting to recruit and manipulate him.
address_pairs.speaker: 알 디아브 자와히리

continuity: Al Diab Jawahiri is the elderly leader of Al-Qaeda and a committed terrorist ideologue who claims Muslims will eventually unite beneath Allah's banner.
Al Diab's underground hideout and its trained defenders have been defeated by the masked protagonist; Al Diab remains in the Skeleton King's custody after losing his wrist.
The Fire Dragon Armor can repel ordinary aura-based attacks and weapons, while Force remains capable of harming opponents protected by lesser defenses.
The Skeleton King can use the corpses of defeated terrorists as materials for his undead army, and the protagonist has accepted this disposition of the dead.
plot: The masked protagonist confronts Al Diab Jawahiri, the leader of Al-Qaeda, in an underground hideout. Al Diab attempts to justify terrorism through religious unity, but the protagonist rejects him, severs his wrist, and defeats the assassins protecting him with the Fire Dragon Armor, Force, and his short sword. The Skeleton King then arrives and prepares to turn the dead terrorists into undead soldiers, which the protagonist accepts because he considers them enemies rather than his own kind.
translation_decisions: Use Al Diab Jawahiri and Al-Qaeda for 알 디아브 자와히리 and 알 카에다.
Retain Fire Dragon Armor, Force, Finger Qi, and grappling technique for the established Murim terminology.
Render 이이제이 as “Fight barbarians with barbarians” and preserve the Line 1 subway reference as a cultural joke.

active_continuity: Al Diab Jawahiri leads Al-Qaeda and advocates forcing Muslims beneath a single religious banner.
The masked protagonist has defeated Al Diab's underground defenders and severed Al Diab's wrist.
The Fire Dragon Armor protects the protagonist from ordinary aura attacks and weapons.
The Skeleton King is converting the defeated terrorists into materials for an undead army with the protagonist's consent.
open_questions: What fate will the Skeleton King ultimately assign to Al Diab and the remaining corpses?
temporary_decisions: Use Al Diab Jawahiri as the full English rendering of 알 디아브 자와히리.
Keep “Fight barbarians with barbarians” for the 이이제이 wordplay.
Retain the Line 1 reference and its explanatory footnote.

names.notes: The terrorist organization led by Al Diab Jawahiri.
Undead ruler who commands a Skeleton army.

profile_creations.personality: He is calm, manipulative, fanatically committed to religious unity, and convinced that his ideology justifies mass suffering.
profile_creations.relationships: He commands Al-Qaeda and opposes the masked young man who attacked his hideout.
profile_creations.role: Al-Diab Jawahiri is the elderly leader of Al-Qaeda and a major terrorist ideologue in the Middle East.
profile_creations.voice: He speaks in a composed, persuasive, and self-righteous manner that collapses into panic when threatened.

profile_creations.personality: He is practical, blunt, and reluctant to perform work he finds distasteful.
profile_creations.relationships: He works with the masked young man and accepts the defeated terrorists as materials for his undead army.
profile_creations.role: The Skeleton King is an undead ruler who commands a Skeleton army and processes corpses into new undead troops.
profile_creations.voice: He speaks casually and theatrically, with irreverent humor even when discussing violence.
